title: Replication spec for The Behavior of Inventories over the Business Cycle: Evidence across Levels of Development
hypothesis: Inventory dynamics vary systematically across levels of development: strongly procyclical and less volatile/persistent in advanced economies vs acyclical and more volatile/persistent at lower income levels; and responses to long-run productivity and financial shocks differ across groups.
sample: Balanced panel of 72 small open economies with complete records for changes in inventories at current prices, GDP at constant and current prices, investment as Gross Fixed Capital Formation, government consumption, imports, exports, population. Filters: period 1993-2022; exclude 6 countries with GDP >2% of world GDP: Germany, United States, France, Italy, Japan, United Kingdom; exclude countries with recurrent institutional instability or constituted after 1993: Mauritania, Slovakia, Togo, North Macedonia; countries classified to most frequent IMF/World Bank group 1993-2022 mode.
method: 1. Collect variables: delta INV_curr, Y constant and Y_curr, I as GFCF, G, M, X, population. Assess statistical discrepancy ratio = |Disc / delta INV_curr|.

2. Deflate delta INV_curr by country implicit GDP deflator to delta INV. Obtain Y_trend via log-quadratic filter, construct ratio = delta INV / Y_trend_{t-1}. Alternative robustness: log-quadratic, HP filter.
3. Build balanced panel 1993-2022, apply exclusion filters above to obtain 72 countries.
4. Classify into 4 groups per IMF and World Bank mode: 24 advanced high-income, 14 high and upper-middle EMDE, 24 lower-middle EMDE, 10 low-income EMDE.

5. Extract cycle: country-specific quadratic filter in levels: delta inv_t / Y_trend_{t-1} = beta0_i + beta1_i t + beta2_i t^2 + epsilon_i,t; epsilon = delta inv_t^c. For other aggregates take log first difference of per capita terms.
6. Compute median volatility, correlations Corr(delta inv^c, delta y/c/i/g/x/m), relative volatilities sigma(delta inv^c)/sigma(delta arg), serial correlation Corr(delta inv^c_t, delta inv^c_{t-1}).
7. Panel unit-root and cointegration tests: IPS in levels, IPS and LLC in first differences, IPS and LLC AIC on balanced-growth ratios c_t-y_t^g and i_t-y_t^g, Pedroni PP and ADF on (y^g,c,i).

8. Long-run productivity shock KPSW identification: X_i,t=[y^g,c,i]' per capita logs, beta'=[-1 1 0; -1 0 1], panel VECM delta X_i,t = mu_i + alpha beta'X_{i,t-1}+ sum Gamma_j delta X_{i,t-j}+u_i,t with pooled alpha Gamma p=1, C(1)=beta_perp[alpha_perp'(I-sum Gamma_j)beta_perp]^-1 alpha_perp', shock_PS_i,t = e_y' C(1) u_i,t e_y'=[1 0 0] sign-normalized to positive long-run output, persistence AR1 with FE clustered SE.

9. Financial shock: BAA spread = yield Baa corporate minus Treasury, instrument with SM_t=sum FF4_j in year t and global uncertainty UNC_t annual average Ludvigson index, estimate BAA_t = gamma0+gamma1 SM_t+gamma2 UNC_t+nu_t, shock = predicted component, diagnostics first-stage F on global annual series, Montiel-Olea-Pflueger effective F per group-horizon clustered by year, Hansen J, Durbin-Wu-Hausman, AR1 persistence.

10. Local projections h=0..5 separately per group and shock: delta inv^c_{i,t+h}=alpha_i+lambda_t+beta_PS_h shock_PS_i,t+Gamma_PS_h Z_{i,t-1}+eps and delta inv^c_{i,t+h}=alpha_i+beta_F_h BAA_hat_t+Gamma_F_h Z_{i,t-1}+eps, Z = 2 lags output growth and 2 lags delta inv^c, clustered SE by country, robust estimator for PS, alternative specs: crisis dummies 1998 2009 2020, 1 vs 2 lags, leave-one-out, year and two-way clustering.
11. LP variance share VS^j_{g,h}=100 * beta^j2_g,h Var_w(tilde s^j_i,t)/Var_w(tilde delta inv^c_{i,t+h}) residualized w.r.t controls and FE, weighted for PS.
